subject: Follow-up: Telemetry hygiene & header/traceID masking — ArtemisCare
messages:
From: Patrick Smith <patrick.smith@artemiscare.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:22:00-04:00
Subject: Follow-up: Logging controls & data residency (ArtemisCare)

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate the clear framing. A couple of clarifying items from our side so Legal and Platform can start internal scoping: 

1) Header suppression: can Redwood suppress arbitrary headers at ingestion per-route (we need to remove X-Client-Phone and X-Internal-Trace)? Is the suppression list configurable per-route or only global?

2) Trace ID handling: we need deterministic pseudonymization so our ops team can correlate sessions across logs but without storing raw IDs in plaintext. Do you support hashing with a customer-provided KMS key, or do you recommend irreversible salt+hash inside Redwood?

3) Retention & access: default suggestion from IT is 7 days raw (encrypted), 90 days pseudonymized index — can Redwood accommodate tiered retention and a legal-hold override?

4) Sampling: we may want a 10% sample of full request/response payloads for debugging, otherwise only metadata. How granular is sampling (per-route, per-customer, or global)?

We've attached a small log sample that contains example headers and traceIDs so you can sketch a proposed config: artemis-log-sample.jsonl (attached).

Next steps from us: Legal wants a one-page summary of options and a proposed pilot configuration. Can you produce that by EOD Tuesday? Also can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive (engineers + security) next week?

Thanks,
Patrick
Head of Platform
ArtemisCare

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Patrick Smith <patrick.smith@artemiscare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Logging controls & data residency (ArtemisCare)

Patrick — thanks for the clear list and the sample. Quick summary and commitments from Redwood: 

- Header suppression: supported. We offer a configurable allowlist and denylist; can be applied globally, per-model, or per-route. For your case we recommend a denylist that includes X-Client-Phone and X-Internal-Trace scoped to production routes.

- Trace ID pseudonymization: two options
  * Deterministic HMAC with customer-managed KMS key (recommended for correlation). We store only the HMACed value; raw traceID never persisted in plaintext.
  * Irreversible salt+hash inside Redwood (no customer key) if you prefer us to manage keys.

- Retention tiers: we can implement 7-day encrypted raw storage + 90-day pseudonymized indices + archival purge. Legal-hold overrides supported — data tagged under hold will be retained and isolated until release.

- Sampling: sampling rules are configurable per-route and per-customer; we can implement a 10% full-payload sampling rule scoped to the debug route you share.

I'm attaching a concise playbook that describes the options and a sample masking config (redwood-telemetry-playbook.pdf). Karthik and Neha will outline technical config and a pilot plan in a follow-up.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive (60m) — suggest Tue 10/20 10:00–11:00 ET or Wed 10/21 14:00–15:00 ET
- Redwood to produce a one-page options summary (target: EOD Tue)
- Pilot: 2-week pilot with sample config + 10% sampling on a staging route

If that aligns we’ll work up the pilot config and a short SOW.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Technical approach + action items for ArtemisCare

Internal notes (do not forward raw):

Summary of proposed technical approach:
- Ingestion pipeline: add header-denylist stage (regex + explicit header names). Denylist evaluated before any storage or indexing.
- TraceID pseudonymization: implement HMAC-SHA256 using customer KMS key via our KMS connector (supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). The connector rotates keys per your policy; we only store HMAC output and a key version tag.
- Raw payload storage: route-level toggle to store raw request/response encrypted in cold tier for up to N days (we recommend 7). Cold tier access requires role-based approval and is audited.
- Pseudonymized index: build a separate index table that retains non-PII metadata + hashed traceIDs for 90 days.
- Sampling: use deterministic hashing on traceID to pick 10% sample (stable across retries) and store full payload for sampled requests only.

Action items (Karthik + Engs):
1) Draft masking-config-example.yaml (include header denylist, route toggles, sampling rate) — deliverable: EOD Mon
2) Prepare a short demo (10 min) showing: a) header suppression in staging, b) HMAC traceID workflow (using test KMS) — deliverable: tech call
3) Confirm EU residency: ensure logs for ArtemisCare prod routes are pinned to eu-central-1 storage — need confirmation from infra team (Neha)

Risks / questions for security:
- Legal asked if Redwood retains any derivable secret after using HMAC — answer: only HMAC outputs and key version; no raw traceIDs. Need Neha to confirm wording for one-pager.

Attachments: masking-config-example.yaml (contains sample denylist + sampling rule).

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Patrick Smith <patrick.smith@artemiscare.com>

- EU residency: ArtemisCare requires prod logs to stay in EU. Can Redwood guarantee eu-central-1 residency for both raw encrypted tier and pseudonymized index?
- SOC2: our auditors require evidence that logging changes are tracked and role-based. Can you include screenshots or audit report snippets in the one-page?
- Pilot timing: Tue 10/20 10:00 ET works for our team (Patrick, two platform engineers, and one in-house security engineer). Please send a calendar invite.

Attachments: none.
